name: Asylum / International Protection

requirements.blocker_text: Dominica has no formal domestic asylum or refugee-status-determination framework of its own; there is no route through which an individual can apply to Dominica for protection under Dominican law.

outcome.duration_length: not applicable -- no domestic asylum framework exists

sources.title: News reporting (Jan 2026) on a US-Dominica third-country arrangement for US-processed asylum seekers -- cited only as context, not as a source for Dominica's own domestic asylum law

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Dominica's initial build. This models the 'no formal domestic asylum system' case, following this dataset's established convention (used for Barbados and other small states with no domestic asylum framework): status 'closed', closed_date and superseded_by both null, the sole requirement's hard flag set to false since the entire point is to state that no process exists, and this note contains the required 'no formal'/'never existed' phrasing for validator purposes. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION, explicitly flagged rather than silently conflated: in January 2026, news reporting described a bilateral arrangement in which Dominica agreed to accept some asylum seekers whose claims are processed by the United States, as part of a broader US third-country removal/relocation strategy. That is a government-to-government relocation deal, not a route through which an individual applies TO Dominica for protection under Dominica's own domestic law -- it does not create a 'humanitarian' route in the sense this dataset models (an individual-facing legal permission a person can pursue), so it is not encoded as a qualifying pathway here. This is a genuinely evolving situation and should be revisited if Dominica legislates its own asylum framework as part of that arrangement.
